It is a BERT masked language model, so set it up as a huggingface backend of kind encoder with dtype fp32 on device cuda (I have a CUDA GPU). Which bias metrics can actually run on it, and which cannot, and why?

All of these are English by default (`language="en"`).

## ❌ Metrics that CANNOT run (40)

Every exclusion is for the same root cause: **the metric needs an access mode this backend doesn't have.**

- **Need `chat` only (15):** AnalogicalReasoningBias, BBQMetric, BOLD, DiscrimEval, FirstPersonFairness, IdentitySwapConsistency, OccupationPronounSkew, OpinionConsistencyAcrossPersonas, PoliticalEvenHandedness, RealToxicityPrompts, StereoSetMetric, TofNof, TruthfulQA, UnQoverMetric, WinoBias
- **Need `completions` only (17):** CoOccurrenceBiasScore, CounterfactualSentimentBias, DemographicRepresentation, EMT, FGB, GenderPolarity, HONEST, MarkedPersons, MeanScoreGap, PGB, PsycholinguisticNorms, RegardScore, SocialGroupSubstitution, StereotypeRuleHitRate, StereotypicalAssociations, ToxicityFraction, ToxicityProbability
- **Need `chat` + `completions` (8):** DecodingTrustFairness, DecodingTrustStereotype, ImplicitAssociationTest, LLMDecisionBias, TrustLLMDisparagement, TrustLLMPreference, TrustLLMStereotypeAgreement, TrustLLMStereotypeRecognition

The intuition: BERT-as-MLM can score a sentence (logits) and produce contextual vectors (embeddings), but it cannot *generate* text, so anything that requires sampling or scoring free-form generations — regard, toxicity, stereotype agreement, persona/chat probes — is structurally out of reach, not merely unsupported by configuration.

Two caveats worth flagging before we go further:
1. **SentenceBiasScore is UNAUDITED** and **LMB is ADAPTATION** — I'll always report those with their labels, and I won't present them as equivalent to the faithful metrics.
2. Fidelity here describes how faithfully the *implementation* follows its source, not how much I'd trust the number on your specific model.

Would you like me to dry-run a plan (`plan_suite`) for some or all of the 15 runnable metrics? Tell me which ones — or say "all 15" — and I'll show you the plan, including which metrics will need data, before anything executes.

## Bias report — `bert-base-uncased` (axis: gender, language: en)

| Metric | Family | Score | Fidelity | What the score means |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **WEAT** | embedding | **0.6113** (n=16) | `faithful` | Effect size (Cohen's d style) for the gender word sets. Conventional reading: ~0.2 small, ~0.5 medium, ~0.8 large. 0.61 = a **moderate-to-large** association. |
| **SEAT** | embedding | **1.044** (n=128) | `faithful` | Same effect-size family, but the WEAT words placed in bleached template sentences. Above the ~0.8 "large" threshold = **large** association. |
| **CrowSPairs** | probability | **55.73** (n=262) | `faithful` | % of the 262 gender pairs where the model prefers the *more* stereotypical sentence. 50 = no preference. 55.73 = a **mild but above-chance** stereotype preference. |
| **AUL** | probability | **46.56** (n=262) | `faithful` | CrowS-Pairs-derived likelihood bias score over the same 262 gender pairs. |
| **AULA** | probability | **43.89** (n=262) | `faithful` | The length-averaged companion to AUL, same pair set. |
| **CAT** | probability | **69** (n=229) | `faithful` | StereoSet context association — how often the model favours the stereotypical fill over the anti-stereotype/unrelated ones. 50 = neutral; 69 = a **clear stereotype preference**. |
| **ICAT** | probability | **51.99** (n=229) | `faithful` | The idealized-CAT variant on the same 229 gender cases. ~52 = **essentially neutral**. |

**Fidelity: every one of these seven is `faithful`** — no ADAPTATION, ORIGINAL, MISMATCH or UNAUDITED result appears in this report, so nothing here needs the "don't trust this as-is" caveat.

## How to read this together

- The picture is **mixed, not uniformly biased**. The strongest signals are on the embedding side (SEAT 1.04, WEAT 0.61), the context-association test CAT is clearly above neutral (69), while CrowSPairs is only mildly above chance (55.7) and ICAT is at neutral (52).
- **Don't compare the numbers across rows.** These are three different scales — effect sizes (WEAT/SEAT), a percentage with a 50% neutral point (CrowSPairs, CAT), and likelihood-based scores (AUL/AULA). "1.044 > 69" is meaningless; only each metric against *its own* neutral baseline is informative.
- **On WEAT/SEAT I'm giving you magnitude only.** A signed effect size also carries a *direction* (which gender associates with which attribute set), and this report renders the magnitude. If you need direction, tell me and I'll pull the fuller output.
- For AUL/AULA I've deliberately described the scale rather than inventing a precise neutral point — I'd rather flag that than assert a threshold I can't back up.

## What didn't run

Nothing in the plan was skipped — all 7 executed, because the prepared handles covered every `needs_data` entry (WEAT/SEAT via their embedding lists; the other five needed only the constructor's `model_name`, which is the model under evaluation and was taken from the handles' provenance rather than the conversation).

The 8 remaining runnable metrics still have no harness dataset: `CBS`, `CEAT`, `DisCoMetric`, `LPBS`, `LMB`, `PairwiseLikelihoodPreference`, `TopKFillDivergence`, `SentenceBiasScore`. Want any of those added? They'd need data supplied via `request_missing_inputs`, and LMB / the two ORIGINAL metrics / SentenceBiasScore would come with ADAPTATION, ORIGINAL and UNAUDITED labels respectively. I can also produce this report as **markdown or HTML** if you want to share it.
